column1: # Quantities that have a canonical source and must never be independently typed
# into manuscript prose. This is a REGISTRY, not a ban on digits: years,
# citation keys, RUCC bands, section numbers, a 95% confidence level and a 60%
# land-share threshold are legitimate literals and are not listed here.
# fmt      how the paper renders it. `n` means a count, matched both as 14,861
#          and 14861. A percentage is matched at the precision it is reported
#          at, because 89.3 and 89.34 are different literals and only the
#          reported one is the one that drifts.
# equals   another key that must carry the same value. Two representations of
#          one estimand may not disagree -- this is the manuscript-side twin of
# why      what breaks if this is typed instead of generated
# NOT LISTED, DELIBERATELY: table1.cm_pct renders as "1" and movers.* render as
# two-digit numbers. A one- or two-character literal matches section numbers,
# RUCC codes and table references, so protecting them would fire constantly on
# correct prose and the gate would be switched off within a week. They are
# generated in the manuscript today; they are simply not enforceable this way.
